grades.quote: A process can access a page only if it has the appropriate permission in its key register and the page table entry also allows the access. Thus, the page table entry can specify the maximum access for any process
grades.reason: Generic OS text explaining that page table entries carry read/write/execute access control bits that set the maximum access for any process. It combines these with per-process protection key registers. It covers page-level permissions but does not discuss user versus supervisor access or give ISA-specific PTE details.
Covers POSIX file permissions (rwx on files and directories) and ACLs, not page-table permissions on memory pages.

grades.quote: The R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively. When one of these bits is clear, the corresponding access type is denied.
grades.reason: Describes RISC-V PMP R/W/X permission bits and the access faults they raise for fetch, load and store. PMP is physical memory protection, not page-table mapping, and the passage has no user-mode or page-table permissions. It is only loosely related auxiliary information.
